questions.q: What does the DORA acronym stand for in DHCP?
options: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge
Domain, Offer, Resolve, Address
Discover, Open, Reply, Assign
Detect, Offer, Register, Authorize
questions.explain: DORA is the four-step DHCP exchange: the client discovers a server, the server offers an address, the client requests it, and the server acknowledges.

questions.q: Why is the client's DHCPDISCOVER sent as a broadcast instead of directly to a specific server?
options: Because the client doesn't have an IP address yet and doesn't know which server(s) exist on the segment
Because broadcasts are always faster than unicast
Because DHCP servers refuse unicast traffic
Because the client is intentionally hiding its MAC address
questions.explain: The client has no IP address yet, so it can't send a normal unicast packet, and it broadcasts so any DHCP server on the local segment can respond.

questions.q: Besides an IP address, what else does a typical DHCP offer include?
options: Only the device's MAC address
Subnet mask, default gateway, DNS server(s), and a lease time
The device's hostname only
A list of every other device's IP address on the network
questions.explain: A DHCP offer is a full configuration bundle: subnet mask, default gateway, DNS servers, and how long the lease is valid (lease time).

questions.q: What typically happens well before a DHCP lease fully expires?
options: The device immediately loses all network connectivity
The device quietly tries to renew the lease directly with the issuing server, usually keeping the same address
The device switches to a static IP automatically
The DHCP server deletes its own configuration
questions.explain: Around the 50% mark of the lease, the device attempts a quiet renewal with the same server, typically keeping its existing address with no visible interruption.

questions.q: Why would a server or a router's management interface typically get a static IP instead of a DHCP-assigned one?
options: Static IPs are required by law for all networking equipment
DHCP cannot technically assign addresses to servers
So the address never changes and other devices can reliably find it at a fixed, predictable address
Static IPs are always faster than DHCP-assigned ones
questions.explain: Devices other systems need to reliably find — servers, printers, network gear — are usually given a static IP so their address stays predictable, unlike DHCP's dynamic assignment.
